The regraded spoils will be tested for pH, conductivity, particle size distribution and selected trace elements prior to placing topsoil on the surface if overburden studies indicate that a problem exists.

Where problems exist in the spoils, a deeper layer of topsoil or other neutral material will be laid down to assure an adequate plant rooting zone.
The spoil surface will be disked to relieve compaction. This will also serve to roughen the spoil surface to reduce erosion and slippage of topsoil.
The topsoil will be analyzed for Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium to determine the proper levels of fertilizer needed. Currently one grab sample is taken for each 2 acres of topsoil.
The grass seed will be drill seeded on the contour when possible.

Broadcast seeding will be utilized when slopes prohibit seeding with the use of agricultural equipment.
Mining Equipment and Facilities
The Sarpy Creek mine is presently producing about 4 million tons of coal per year using one 75-cubic yard dragline. To reach a production level of 10 million tons per year, an additional dragline of 110-cubic yard capacity will be obtained. These two machines will be sufficient for the proposed 20-year plan. Coal is loaded with 18-cubic yard front-end loaders into 100-ton bottom-dump trucks for transport to the processing facilities. Motorized scrapers are used to remove and redistribute topsoil, and bulldozers are used for cleaning the top of the coal and for leveling and grading spoil piles. Overburden and coal drills would be used for drilling the overburden and coal preparatory to blasting.
